A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DreamCatalyst with the same authors and core framework. All 13 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, tables and figures. v1 ends with references; v2 includes appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original NeRF editing comparisons, quantitative metrics, human preferences and qualitative ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original NeRF results and reports additional 3DGS comparisons, quantitative ablations and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The default identity-regularized DDS objective, decreasing timesteps, FreeU and IP2P guidance are retained. v2 adds two alternative DDS weighting functions and a GaussianEditor-integrated variant with a densification cutoff (Section 3.3 and Appendix B.2), extending the procedure without replacing its core.

E1.justification: Both versions report eight scenes and 40 prompt pairs from IN2N/PDS data. Figure 15 adds a limited input-condition scenario comparing simple and detailed prompts alongside the corresponding 2D-IP2P failure. The larger 3DGS evaluation primarily changes model configurations within the retained scene-editing coverage.

E2.justification: The NeRF comparison retains IN2N and PDS. The new 3DGS comparison evaluates GaussianEditor with DDS and IN2N guidance, plus DGE (Table 2 and Figure 8). These are substantial additions to the evaluated comparator set; DGE was only cited in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 introduces separate Nerfstudio/splatfacto and Threestudio 3DGS protocols, with method-specific training budgets and densification settings. The reported user-study sample changes from 50 to 100 participants, and the prompt-alignment question drops its quality requirement. These are reported protocol revisions; unchanged preference percentages do not establish that the study was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative FreeU ablations, alternative-weight sensitivity tests, additional FreeU examples and an IP2P/prompt-specificity failure analysis. It removes v1's controlled 500-iteration random-versus-decreasing-timestep comparison for DreamCatalyst. Appendix C.1 instead tests PDS with decreasing timesteps, answering a different question.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 5's linear-regression trend lines with 95% confidence bands. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates for the tabulated scores or significance tests. The participant-count revision concerns study sample size rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises retained NeRF scores: PDS CLIP directional similarity changes from 0.174 to 0.161, while the fast mode changes from 0.158 to 0.165, reversing their order. v2 adds 3DGS, weighting-variant, quantitative FreeU and failure-case results. NeRF timings and user-preference percentages remain unchanged. The score revisions are unexplained and cannot be treated as demonstrated method improvements.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly defines the DDIM noise coefficient from the schedule and changes the stated PDS noise-scale factor from beta_t to 1-alpha_t in Section 2. It also defines two additional weighting functions. The central DDS/SDEdit derivation is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the headline contribution from NeRF editing to model-agnostic editing with claimed state-of-the-art results on both NeRF and 3DGS. The earlier priority claim about adopting decreasing timesteps for general 3D editing is dropped. The central diffusion-sampling and FreeU contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability and failure explanations: inherited IP2P prompt-following failures, improvement through detailed prompts, and segmentation/projection mismatch attributed to GE/DGE errors (Appendices C.2 and F.1). It also interprets the alternative-weight results as robustness to the precise coefficient choice, extending v1's discussion of the identity/editability trade-off.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports an official code repository, 3DGS implementation recipes, the complete evaluation prompt list and survey details including vigilance filtering, shared camera trajectories and randomized options. Existing NeRF and guidance details move to Appendix B. However, v1's timestep range [0.2, 0.9] and statement about retaining FreeU's original skip-feature scaling settings disappear.

R1.justification: v2 substantially develops positioning against model-specific GaussianEditor/DGE approaches and explicitly distinguishes its interpretation from DreamSampler's source–target equality assumption. It adds citations including DDS, GaussianEditor, 3DGS, Threestudio and DreamGaussian, while removing InstructHumans and the associated discussion of earlier decreasing-timestep editing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten and reorganized. SDEdit preliminaries, text guidance and implementation details move into appendices; the preliminary and experimental subsections are restructured. New appendix organization and an ethics statement further change the document's narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds 3DGS and FreeU result tables, a full prompt table, comparison grids, survey screenshots and a limitations figure. Figure 2 gains weighting curves; Figure 6 replaces the FreeU examples and removes the timestep-ablation row. Existing displays are also relocated and resized, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility beyond v1's NeRF-only comparisons and qualitative component ablations. The 3DGS evaluations, quantitative FreeU and weighting tests, detailed prompts and implementation information, and illustrated IP2P limitation make the method more assessable. Unexplained score and participant-count revisions, removal of the original scheduling ablation, and lost setting disclosures are weaknesses, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
